newsitem.title: UK: UK aims to limit liability of professional firms.
newsitem.headline: UK aims to limit liability of professional firms.

text.p: The government said on Thursday it intended to bring forward legislation to make limited liability partnerships (LLP) available to regulated professions in Britain.

The decision marks a victory for bodies representing accountants, solicitors, engineers, surveyors and others who have expressed growing concern that the law on joint and several liability was exposing them to expensive litigation over claims for which they were only partly responsible.
Trade Secretary Ian Lang said he would publish detailed proposals for legislation before Easter.

The issue has come to a head because two of the Big Six accounting firms have said they plan to move their registered offices offshore to Jersey, whose parliament last month passed a law permitting LLP.
Accounting firms have been especially hard hit by large negligence claims, and KPMG has already incorporated its auditing arm as a way of limiting liability.

Lang said in a written parliamentary answer that he was well aware of the concerns within professions about the consequences of the unlimited liability of partners in the modern commercial environment.

"In a big modern partnership advising on large commercial transactions it may be impossible for partners to know all other partners and their work -- yet their personal assets can be put at risk by the actions of their partners," Lang said.
"The government is determined to maintain a competitive and up-to-date legal framework for business in the UK," he added.
Legislation would be subject to appropriate safeguards to protect the interests of those doing business with LLPs.
To keep a level playing field, LLPs registered abroad but operating in the UK will have to file financial information equivalent to that required from UK registered LLPs, Lang added.

Lang acknowledged that Jersey and the United States were amending their partnership laws and said responses to a recent consultation by his department were strongly in favour of dealing with the issue.
The Confederation of British Industry and 18 professional bodies wrote to the government on Wednesday calling for a change in the law.

"We are seriously concerned that the UK will become increasingly out of step to the detriment of our international competitiveness," the letter said. The CBI was not immediately available to comment on Lang's proposal.
